source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Aurora is Illinois' largest disclosed data center campus at 114 megawatts, representing 48 percent of the state's published IT capacity.

The campus spans 450,000 square feet across three buildings, yielding about 6.3 megawatts per 10,000 square feet, a density typical of hyperscale colocation built in the last decade. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 114 megawatts translates to roughly 2,850 racks.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, but only six publish power figures. This campus accounts for nearly half of the state's disclosed IT capacity, so any statewide estimate of compute potential rests heavily on one operator's public specification.

The published record omits total campus power draw, PUE, renewable sourcing, grid connection characteristics, and interconnect uplinks. Without those facts, the campus's ability to support AI training depends on undisclosed constraints: local grid capacity, cooling thermal density, and backbone connectivity. Green Globes certification addresses environmental impact accounting but not power delivery tier or redundancy topology.
